answer: Price sybils out with scarce identity seats: a fixed supply sold by recurring second-price auction, each seat carrying a continuous Harberger rent. Standing seats are as limited as old-growth timber, so every clone must win one at the clearing price and keep paying as the bidding tide rises. A thousand fakes owe a thousand perpetual rents, while an honest agent's single hard-won seat stays rare as a pearl, and the farm bleeds dry before it can sway any vote.
